Defective rival-rejection warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with the qinah-style exclamation אֵיכָה֙ (oshb:Isa.1.21, byte tier), “How the faithful city has become a prostitute!” (web:Isa.1.21), a fresh lament-onset distinct from the preceding conditional oracle. Between the brackets, verse 24 pivots on the stacked title-and-signature נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.1.24, byte tier), “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says” (web:Isa.1.24); this hoy, ה֚וֹי, is a divine self-exclamation over Yahweh's own coming action, not a woe pronounced against the addressee, so it is read as an internal turn within the bracketed lament-to-restoration unit rather than a row-cutting seam. Verse 20, which closes just before this row opens, carries its own setumah break (oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration).

current_row.boundary_rationale: Opens with צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, byte tier), “Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.” (web:Isa.1.27), shifting from the first-person ‘I will’ divine speech of 1:24-26 to third-person declarative summary naming Zion's redeemed and the apostates' fate side by side, a discourse-mode shift read as the row's opening seam. They will both burn” (oshb:Isa.1.31), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), and before the fresh ha-davar superscription opening chapter 2.

items.claim: The row's only opening-seam driver is a Hebrew form-class claim - a first-person to third-person discourse-mode shift - argued with no pointed splice of the verb forms it rests on.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes. וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה opens oshb:Isa.1.26 (token 1 of 13, byte tier) and תִּפָּדֶ֑ה stands at oshb:Isa.1.27 (token 3 of 5, byte tier): the first-to-third-person shift claim is byte-true, and strongest_rejected_alternative concedes the 26|27 seam 'is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker'. One correction to the finding's grounds: the third-person verb IS spliced in the row - צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, tokens 1-3, byte tier) opens boundary_rationale - so 'neither form is spliced anywhere in the row' overstates. The defect nonetheless stands as filed: that splice is presented as the row's opening quotation, never as the pointed ground of the person claim; the shift's first-person pole is spliced nowhere in any field of the row (re-checked across the full row text); the seam's label is carried by the English rendering of 1:24-26; and the only pointed cross-seam evidence the row offers is the righteousness catchword it honestly reports as pulling toward continuity. Under the engagement-class law - pointed splices with tiers mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, form-class labels under digit discipline - a sole-driver mode-shift seam with its contrast pair unspliced is a defective warrant, and the row's medium_low confidence with the frontier flag is the honest calibration of exactly that gap. Medium as filed.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes, adversarially both ways. The opening verse is three tokens in full, "וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף" (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier, collate-verified): a waw-conjunctive definite noun phrase carrying no hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative, or temporal-formula onset; the staged parashah inventory carries no seg at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18 (nearest segs: SAMEKH at Isa.2.11, PE at Isa.2.22, single witness, tier-3), so the 2:17|2:18 seam has neither a tier-1 onset nor a tier-3 mark, absence weighed only as absence of support. readjudication.grounds: Both sides re-derived from bytes. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): the refrain clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא closes oshb:Isa.2.17 (byte tier) and recurs byte-identically as the close of oshb:Isa.2.11 (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier, and 2 at skeleton — the only two sites in the book); the two stanzas it closes each open on a ruled onset — the vocative-plus-imperative summons בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה at oshb:Isa.2.5 (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse skeleton) and the temporal-formula onset כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת at oshb:Isa.2.12 (byte tier; sweep: 1 verse skeleton) — so the refrain's bracket function is argued from bytes at both sites, and under the strategy's refrain-close rule (refrains close units; a refrain that byte-recurs at the close of successive stanzas brackets each stanza) the 2:17|2:18 seam is warranted from the left by a ruled tier-1 CLOSE. RIGHT: וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier, the whole verse) carries no ruled onset class — the finding's onset-only reading re-derives exactly — but a waw-prefixed opener is not counterevidence to a seam: the accepted onsets וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא at oshb:Isa.7.18 and וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י at oshb:Isa.11.1 (both byte tier) are waw-prefixed. Tier-3: the staged parashah inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.2.11 and PE at Isa.2.22 and no seg at Isa.2.17 or Isa.2.18 (single witness; absence weighed as nothing). The filed claim that 'the warrant is topical shift alone' therefore fails the complete test: the shipped row grounds its opening on 'the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17' and 'the refrain-closed catalogue' and cites web:Isa.2.17 and web:Isa.2.5-Isa.2.17 — the row weighed the left side; the finding did not. The prior adjudication applied the no-tier-1-at-own-seam rule from the opening verse alone and treated the refrain as context rather than as the ruled close; the both-sides law reverses that outcome. The continuity facts the finding cites do not erase the close: the four-token flight core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר collates byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 1 verse byte, 3 verses accent_stripped), and the idols lexeme stands at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (אֱלִילִ֑ים, אֱלִילֵ֣י, byte tier; sweep: 8 verses skeleton book-wide, 3 in this chapter) — both motifs bind 2:18-22 to the FIRST stanza (2:5-11) across the whole of 2:12-17, so they straddle the 2:11 refrain close exactly as they straddle the 2:17 one; they argue the poem-level envelope over 2:5-22 that the neighbour row already discloses as a rival, not a merger of 2:18-22 with 2:12-17. The verse-initial temporal formula בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ at oshb:Isa.2.20 (byte tier; bare-form sweep: 45 verses skeleton) is an in-unit formula two verses past a seam already warranted from the left. Residual defect, real but low: the row engages its load-bearing left-side warrant by reference only — no oshb:Isa.2.17 in boundary_evidence_refs, no spliced refrain bytes or tier label in its own fields (the byte-tier splice lives only in the neighbour row), no refrain.* signal key in observed_substrate_signals, and its rejected-alternative sentence restates the bound as 'topical shift ... and the petuchah break', leaning on a tier-3 mark and omitting the tier-1 close — an engagement-class and field-contract gap, not a missing warrant; confidence medium is defensible, and the high-confidence aggravator that sets this class at medium elsewhere is absent. Span ruling: decline the routing proposal. Branch (a), Isa.2.12-Isa.2.22, would erase a refrain-closed boundary while leaving the byte-identical 2:11 close standing, and shows from no byte why the refrain closes a unit at 2:11 but not at 2:17; the motifs it would lean on bind 2:18-22 to 2:5-11, not to 2:12-17. Branch (b), Isa.2.20-Isa.2.22, is byte-unsound: it severs the eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, byte-identical at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses byte tier), and leaves 2:18-19 as a tail closing on nothing. Branch (c)'s 'tier-1 shortfall at the opening seam' does not exist under the complete test. The span Isa.2.18-Isa.2.22 stands — warranted at its front by the 2:17 refrain close and at its rear by the imperative close חִדְל֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מִן הָ֣אָדָ֔ם at oshb:Isa.2.22 (byte tier; sweep: 2 verses skeleton for the imperative) with PE corroboration and the fresh hinneh-announcement onset כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier). The cure is a field repair (splice and tier-label the 2:17 refrain, add oshb:Isa.2.17, add a refrain.* key, re-cut the rejected-alternative sentence so the bound is the refrain close with the PE as corroboration), and the adjacent row Isa.2.12-Isa.2.17 is ruled coherently: its refrain close stands.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A third-person narrative frame opens the row: "וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Isa.7.1, byte tier), matching “In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.” (web:Isa.7.1) -- a clean scene shift from the throne-vision report. Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span without reopening it: "וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒" (oshb:Isa.7.3, byte tier), matching “Then Yahweh said to Isaiah” (web:Isa.7.3); "כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.7.7, byte tier), matching “This is what the Lord Yahweh says” (web:Isa.7.7); "וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Isa.7.10, byte tier), matching “Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz, saying,” (web:Isa.7.10); and "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier), matching “Listen now, house of David” (web:Isa.7.13). These four stand inside the third-person narrative frame opened at web:Isa.7.1 rather than beside it, so the frame owns the embedded speech and nothing among the four reopens the row; the same narrative frame does not extend past its own close, which is why its defective-spelled resumptive twin at oshb:Isa.8.5 opens a fresh row rather than continuing this one. The frame runs through the Immanuel sign to its closing threat, “Yahweh will bring on you, on your people, and on your father’s house days that have not come, from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria.” (web:Isa.7.17), where the next verse’s repeated “in that day” formula (web:Isa.7.18) opens a different oracle cycle. The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself: the narrated direct-address scene that has framed the intervening speech since web:Isa.7.1 gives way here to an impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative cuts the Immanuel sign (web:Isa.7.14-Isa.7.16) into its own servant_song-type row separate from the Ahaz narrative, but no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene, so frame-plus-speech is kept as one larger unit.

Both sides re-derived. LEFT (this row's own close): oshb:Isa.7.17 closes the named-participant scene in direct second-person address — יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ (byte tier) carries three 2ms pronominal suffixes (a suffix scan of oshb:Isa.7.17 finds exactly these three) — and the staged parashah inventory records PE at Isa.7.17 (single witness, tier-3 corroboration only). RIGHT (the following unit's onset): וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא opens oshb:Isa.7.18 verse-initially (byte tier), a formula onset of the class the neighbouring rows treat as a driver (the extended form sweeps 5 verses at byte tier and 13 at accent_stripped, oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 among the 13; the bare in-that-day skeleton 45 verses), and the person shifts at the seam itself from 2ms address to third-person announcement, יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), with no 2nd-person pronominal suffix anywhere in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 (suffix scan: 0 hits). The seam is therefore warranted from BOTH sides by byte-true ruled signals that the row itself already splices and cites — which is why the finding and the prior adjudication agree the placement is not the defect. What the complete test changes is the weight of the defect. The row's load-bearing clause is two-part: (i) a frame-mode shift 'at MT 7:18 itself' — byte-true at the seam (three 2ms suffixes at 7:17 against none at 7:18; a narrated scene with a named addressee giving way to an unaddressed announcement); (ii) a cycle-wide generalisation that 7:18-25 'names no speaker and addresses no one directly'. 'Names no speaker' holds: the divine-speech census places no koh-amar, neum, or amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH site anywhere in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 (nearest: the divine frame at oshb:Isa.7.7 and the narrative onset וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.8.1, byte tier). 'Addresses no one directly' is byte-OPEN, not byte-false: the sole candidate is תָב֣וֹא inside לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier), a qal imperfect whose 2ms and 3fs forms are identical in the pointed bytes; no morphology layer is staged, so the parse cannot be machine-settled, and the 3fs parse — the feminine construct noun that follows as its subject, 'the fear of briers and thorns shall not come there' — is byte-available and is paralleled by יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה in the preceding verse (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), the third-person 'one comes there'. The row's own second witness renders it second person — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — while rendering the cycle's two other taw-prefixed forms, תִּסְפֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) and תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), as third person; the row quotes that rendering and neither argues the parse nor reconciles it. Under the tier-disclosure standard a form-class claim is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses; as shipped the clause is unsupported and witness-contradicted, and against the facing row's 'addressed to the same audience' / 'the four share one addressee' (where 'addressee' means the oracle's target, not a grammatical addressee) the two rows are terminologically inconsistent. The prior adjudication applied the byte-false-load-bearing-warrant rule, testing the characterisation at the cycle's far end (7:25) and treating the demoted formula as if absent; on the complete test the load-bearing kernel (the shift at the seam) is byte-true, sound warrants stand on both sides in the row's own splices, and the defective part is an over-extended, unargued generalisation plus the row's inverted ordering ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own' — a first-site formula onset does discriminate: nothing of the class stands at oshb:Isa.7.17). A defective load-bearing warrant over a byte-sound, twice-warranted seam is the medium class of this queue (defective warrant, boundary uncontested), not high. Downgrade to medium. Cure as proposed, no span change: delete the 'addresses no one directly' clause, re-argue the rear seam from the 7:17 second-person close and the 7:18 formula onset with the PE as tier-3 corroboration, and align the two rows' 'addressee' wording.

items.claim: "Four verse-initial speech onsets punctuate the span" is a digit whose swept object is unnamed and which is short for the object as stated.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: name the object (e.g. "four verse-initial divine-frame speech onsets") or restate the digit to include MT 7:12. No span change.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived: oshb:Isa.7.12 opens verse-initial on "וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז" (byte tier, collate-verified) — a fifth verse-initial speech onset inside the span, unnamed by the row — and oshb:Isa.7.2 opens on the report formula "וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר" (byte tier). A first-token scan of oshb:Isa.7.1-Isa.7.17 confirms the unqualified class 'verse-initial speech onsets' counts five vayomer/koh-amar/resumptive-speech onsets (7:3, 7:7, 7:10, 7:12, 7:13) even before the 7:2 report formula is weighed, while the four the row names (oshb:Isa.7.3, 7.7, 7.10, 7.13) are the divine/prophetic frame onsets — the object that needed naming under the campaign's semantic-class count discipline, which requires the swept object named before the digit. Medium is right: the digit is not load-bearing — the royal reply at 7:12 sits inside the same third-person narrative frame and reopens nothing — so this is a defective digit-object claim, cured by naming the object or restating the digit, exactly as proposed.

items.claim: The rejected alternative is set aside on the ground that "no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene", but the row's own splices place a ruled tier-1 vocative-imperative onset immediately before the sign speech.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: restrict the ground to the exact cut the rival proposes (web:Isa.7.13|web:Isa.7.14 and web:Isa.7.16|web:Isa.7.17), or re-argue the dismissal from the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule. No span change.
items.adjudicator_grounds: The row's own splices defeat the blanket ground. "וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד" stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.7.13 (byte tier, collate-verified): speech formula plus imperative plus vocative — a shim'u call, a ruled tier-1 onset class in this book's frame spine — and the addressee shifts across it from the 2ms suffix of "שְׁאַל לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת" (oshb:Isa.7.11, byte tier; “Ask a sign of Yahweh your God;” (web:Isa.7.11), the king addressed singular) to the 2mp suffix of "הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙" (oshb:Isa.7.13, byte tier; “Is it not enough for you” (web:Isa.7.13), the house of David addressed plural) — suffix-form readings argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, no morphology layer being staged. So 'no tier-1 frame or addressee shift separates the sign speech from the surrounding narrative scene' is contradicted by the row's own cited evidence for the speech complex that carries the sign; the ground survives only if restricted to the rival's exact cut, where oshb:Isa.7.14 opens on "לָ֠כֵן" (byte tier), a continuation particle rather than a fresh frame — which is what the proposed restriction records. Medium is right: the span itself holds under the frame-plus-speech default-larger-unit rule; only the stated ground fails.
